title: Throughput margin calibration — optimization spreadsheet + recommended settings (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This memo proposes a concise spreadsheet-driven recipe and a small set of recommended runtime knobs to calibrate throughput margins across mixed conversational workloads. The goal: maximize batching and cache utilization while keeping p95/p99 latency inside SLO with a minimal safety buffer. This is an operational-first draft for rapid experiments and subsequent codification into the Optimize presets.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We propose a two-stage calibration: (1) an offline sweep using a lightweight cost model spreadsheet to find Pareto points for batch_size, max_group_delay_ms, cache_ttl_seconds and quantization profile per model family; and (2) a tight online A/B rollout with canary traffic that measures quality regressions (embedding/LM metrics) and tail latency. Early guidance: target effective batch sizes of 6-12 for interactive chat SLO=150ms p95 on GPU instances with 16GB KV cache; set cache_ttl=30–120s for session-heavy apps (higher TTL when turn-taking is frequent), and prefer symmetric INT8 for gpt-like decoder-only models when quality loss <=0.5% measured on a small eval set.

Why this is different:
- Focus on a throughput margin (the difference between observed p95 and SLO) instead of absolute batching presets. That margin determines how aggressive batching can be without impacting SLA.
- Spreadsheet-first: operators can iterate quickly without running full experiments; we tie spreadsheet outputs to a minimal experiment plan.

Key knobs and recommended starting ranges (per-model-family):
- batch_size_target (per-worker grouping): 4, 8, 12, 16 (start at 8)
- max_group_delay_ms (how long to wait to form a batch): 8ms, 16ms, 32ms (start at 16ms for balanced latency/throughput)
- cache_ttl_seconds (prefix/KV cache): 15, 30, 60, 120 (session-heavy get longer TTL)
- cache_eviction_policy: LRU (default) or size-based cap (limit KV mem to 30% of GPU ram)
- quant_profile: none (fp16), int8-symmetric-per-channel (weights), int8-activation-dp (if supported); fallback to fp16 if quality delta > threshold
- quant_quality_threshold: 0.5% relative score delta on eval set (configurable)
- fallback_route: lower-quant or smaller-batch variant with no-cache miss penalty

Compact cost model spreadsheet (column descriptions + example row):
Columns: model, hw_type, base_latency_ms_per_token, tokens_per_request_avg, avg_request_length_tokens, baseline_cost_per_hour_usd, batch_size, effective_tokens_per_second, p95_latency_ms, cache_hit_rate, q_profile, estimated_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, quality_delta_pct
Example row (text CSV):
"gpt-base", "A100-40GB", "0.65", "40", "60", "6.40", "8", "8000", "132", "0.45", "int8-sym", "3.2", "0.3"
Notes on formulae used in sheet: effective_tokens_per_second = (batch_size * tokens_per_request_avg) / (base_latency_ms_per_token * seq_factor + batch_overhead_ms) where seq_factor is 1 + avg_request_length_tokens / 512 (rough estimate). estimated_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd derives from baseline_cost_per_hour_usd scaled by effective_tokens_per_second and instance-hours. This is intentionally conservative—multiply by (1 + safety_margin_pct) where safety_margin_pct is derived from desired throughput margin.

Calibration sweep plan (offline):
1) Select 3 representative workloads: short-chat (avg len 32), medium-dialogue (avg 120), long-form (~512).
2) For each workload/model/hw pair: run microbench to measure base_latency_ms_per_token and batch overhead at batch_size {4,8,12,16}. Record p50/p95/p99.
3) Populate spreadsheet and compute cost per 1M tokens and projected p95 under target batch settings.
4) Choose 2 Pareto-optimal configs per workload (one latency-lean, one cost-lean).
5) Run end-to-end quality checks (prompt eval suite) for chosen quantization profiles.

Online rollout plan (short):
- Canary 5% traffic -> measure p95/p99, cache_hit_rate, warm vs cold ratio, quality checks (20 prompts). If p95 margin < target or quality_delta > threshold, rollback.
- Ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with success gates.
- Safety gates: if p99 increases by >30ms or error rate >0.5% revert automatically.

Observability and metrics to capture:
- per-route: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, batch_size distribution, max_group_delay histogram
- runtime: KV cache hit rate (global + per-route), cold_start ratio, mem pressure on GPU, quant-fallback count
- quality: eval suite score delta, embedding-cosine mean on holdout queries

Acceptance criteria for a config:
- p95 <= SLO and p99 within SLO + 2x safety margin
- cost per 1M tokens reduced vs baseline by >= 8% for cost-lean config
- quality_delta_pct <= quant_quality_threshold
- cache_hit_rate > 30% for session-heavy routes

Quick reference recommended defaults for quick experiments: (do not use in production without sweep)
- interactive chat SLO 150ms p95: batch_size 8, max_group_delay_ms 12–16, cache_ttl 30s, quant_profile int8-sym if quality checks pass
- high-throughput non-interactive (SLO 500ms p95): batch_size 12–16, max_group_delay_ms 24–32, cache_ttl 60–120s, int8 with per-channel weights

Open questions / next steps:
- Decide canonical eval metrics for quality across model families (we currently mix embedding-cosine and n-gram measures)
- Automate spreadsheet ingestion to experiment harness and produce flags for rollout
- Small UX ask: add a UI for live throughput-margin visualization in Console (p95 minus SLO over time)

Appendix: quick checklist for running the sweep
- Identify workloads and collect 1k representative requests each
- Microbench for base latency and batch overhead (3 runs per batch size)
- Fill spreadsheet and mark Pareto frontier
- Run 1000 eval prompts against quant profiles
- Schedule canary for off-peak hour

Responsible: Aisha (owner), Marco (bench harness), Liang (cost-sheet formulas), Priya (quality evals)
